prize_parts.citation: For the lipid self-assembly and ionizable-lipid nanoparticle chemistry that enabled delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a chemistry achievement in the strict sense: the Vancouver work (Cullis, Hope, Madden) rests on lipid phase behaviour, pH-dependent charge and nonbilayer structure, and on controlled assembly of lipid-nucleic acid particles. That physical-chemical understanding converted nucleic-acid drugs from laboratory reagents into medicines. Independent confirmation is overwhelming (patisiran, the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, many later products), and the carrier is the part of the mRNA story that the 2023 Medicine prize did not recognise. I keep this first after reading the colleagues' ballots, because nothing there displaces its combination of originality, maturity and demonstrated human impact.
statement.case_against: Credit is genuinely contested. The Anderson/Langer lipidoid line and industrial developers such as MacLachlan have claims, and a three-name cap forces omissions. The committee may also read this as pharmaceutics or medicine rather than chemistry. Only one member ranked it first, and it sits in the middle of the opening support table. I am also the member closest to lipid self-assembly, so I may overrate how central the physical chemistry was to the engineering that actually delivered the products.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (PROTACs and molecular glues) is a general new drug modality that also explained thalidomide-class drugs, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the core, though the three-name cap forces hard omissions.
responses.response: I agree the concept is original and chemically rich, and B026 is my first alternative. My reservation is maturity and allocation: no PROTAC drug is approved, and the PROTAC strand (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and the cereblon glue strand (Handa, Ito) would each need recognition, which a three-person cap does not accommodate cleanly. Lipid nanoparticles have the opposite profile, with clinical validation at global scale and a tighter core group. I would revisit B026 in a few years, when approvals settle the question.

responses.point: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling by Buchwald and Hartwig is mature, general and ubiquitous in medicinal and process chemistry, with Kosugi a precursor; the funnel energy-landscape theory is his second choice.
responses.response: The scientific case for B065 is strong and the two-laureate allocation is clean, which is a real advantage over my pick. My hesitation is that it is the 2010 cross-coupling prize extended by a closely related bond construction, and its impact is indirect: it makes many molecules easier, whereas lipid nanoparticles created a new class of medicines. I accept that this is a judgment about significance and not a flaw in his argument, and I keep B065 as my second alternative. On B032, I share his worry that the 2024 prize on structure prediction and design overlaps this territory.

responses.point: C-N cross-coupling is overdue after more than thirty years, with fully understood mechanism and a fair Buchwald/Hartwig split; photoredox catalysis (Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz) is a mature, widely adopted second choice.
responses.response: I take the point that thirty years of confirmation, industrial scale and a clean attribution make B065 low-risk. I disagree that overdue-ness by itself should outrank a newer achievement that is just as thoroughly confirmed. The mRNA vaccines and siRNA drugs have had independent validation since 2018 and 2020. I also note that his own photoredox candidate has the opposite attribution problem, with at least seven credited names and a priority dispute over the 2008-2011 reports.

responses.point: Massively parallel sequencing is a chemistry-driven technology (reversible terminators, clonal surface amplification) with exceptional impact, with Balasubramanian and Klenerman as the clear core and Mayer a defensible third.
responses.response: The impact argument is unanswerable, and I ranked B037 fourth. I differ on two points. First, the Sanger prize of 1980 and the earlier sequencing-related recognition (1980, 2002) makes it harder to see a sequencing prize as a new recognition of chemistry rather than of platform technology. Second, the attribution is contested between Solexa, 454 pyrosequencing and the clonal-array lines, and he proposes Mayer while others propose Balasubramanian and Klenerman only. That contest looks as unsettled as the lipid one, so it does not give B037 an allocation advantage over B045.

responses.point: C-N coupling is first because of its unambiguous durable impact, while sequencing by synthesis comes second; he notes that Pd cross-coupling already won in 2010 and that a Liu-only base editing prize is more plausible than a trainee trio.
responses.response: His own caveat about 2010 is the point I weigh most: the committee would be recognising a second palladium coupling prize in 16 years. I agree with his point that attribution inside B004 is better handled by a Liu-centred award, and that is a fair argument against treating any trainee trio as automatic. It also shows that an award with a clear leader is not available for B045, but the Vancouver trio is a principled set because it is defined by the lipid and formulation principles, not by seniority.

uncertainties: Whether the exact division of credit between the Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden), the Anderson/Langer lipidoid line and MacLachlan can be settled from the record available to the committee.
Whether the majority will treat lipid nanoparticle delivery as chemistry given the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification.
Whether a two-part prize, for example pairing this with another shortlisted candidate, would be more defensible than a single three-person award.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to Cullis, Hope or Madden is apparent from my profile. My research field (lipid self-assembly and lipid-protein interaction) is adjacent to B045, and I share a Lund affiliation with committee colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, so I flag the field proximity for transparency; I do not judge that recusal is required.
